entities.summary: The Mukje Conference was held on 1–3 August 1943 in Mukaj. There was signed the Mukje agreement, a treaty between the nationalist Balli Kombëtar and the National Liberation Movement representatives. The aim was to generate a platform on how to regulate the Albanian resistance in World War II and how to prepare for the future of Ethnic Albanian state. The National Liberation Movement included the Communists and Legaliteti of Abaz Kupi, as well as smaller local nationalist leaders. The conference was intermediated by the British emissaries with the idea of unifying the Albanian political spectrum against the Fascists, similar to AVNOJ in Yugoslavia.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Mukje Agreement played a crucial role in unifying Albanian nationalist groups against Fascist forces during World War II, setting the stage for the country's post-war independence. The agreement led to increased cooperation between the National Liberation Movement and Balli Kombëtar, ultimately contributing to Albania's liberation from Italian occupation.
